slides.lead: "the guest is a gift" is a real rule here.
slides.headline:
the safe little capital
nobody books *first*
slides.body: five reasons georgia is a great first solo trip. save this post.

slides.head: why women travel here *alone*
slides.body: crime is low, prices are tiny, and guests are treated like family. hospitality is almost a religion here.

slides.head: the old town fits in *one walk*
slides.body: cobblestones, carved wooden balconies and sulfur baths - all close together, all on foot.

slides.head: the best *view*
slides.body: ride the cable car up to narikala fortress. the whole city lies under your feet.

slides.head: a tip most people *miss*
slides.body: skip taxis. the metro costs cents - and the bathhouse district is the local secret for a slow afternoon.

slides.head: one *easy* day trip
slides.body: mtskheta is 30 minutes away. ancient churches, the old capital - and you are back by lunch.

slides.lead: five simple tips. one easier trip.
